feedback.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
2{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+22t{y}^{′}+50y=0,\,t>0.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}+22t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}+50{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ 2\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }+22\lambda {t}^{\lambda }+50{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[2\lambda (\lambda -1)+22\lambda +50] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\lambda (\lambda -1)+22\lambda +50 & =0 \\ 2{\lambda }^{2}+20\lambda +50 & =0 \\ 2({\lambda }^{2}+10\lambda +25) & =0 \\ 2(\lambda +5)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =-5.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(t)={c}_{1}{t}^{-5}+{c}_{2}{t}^{-5}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.
$$
